problem: The comparison with 3+1 dimensions gives a wrong reason. It says the difference from ordinary Dirac theory is 'the pairing lambda -> -lambda produced by the chirality, which anticommutes with the time gamma'. In 3+1 dimensions gamma5 also anticommutes with gamma0. The real difference is that the invariant form G commutes with the chirality in (4,4), because C is an even product of four gammas. In 3+1 the Dirac form G = gamma0 anticommutes with gamma5, so X = G gamma0 = 1 commutes with gamma5 and no pairing arises.
evidence: Line 3445: '(In ordinary 3+1 dimensions the analogous density psi^dagger psi is positive; the difference is the pairing lambda -> -lambda produced by the chirality, which anticommutes with the time gamma.)' The proof in the same section uses two facts: G commutes with Gamma ('C is a product of four gammas, so it commutes with Gamma') and gamma^(x4) anticommutes with Gamma. Only the first fact fails in 3+1.
fix: Replace the parenthesis by: 'In 3+1 dimensions the invariant form is G = gamma^0, which anticommutes with gamma_5, so the density G gamma^0 = 1 commutes with gamma_5 and is positive; in (4,4) the invariant forms C P_+- commute with Gamma while gamma^(x4) anticommutes with it, and this produces the pairing lambda -> -lambda.'
